claims.text: The initial material is single-phase ZrB2 ceramic.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires a preparation temperature above 2300 °C.
SPS is a non-conventional alternative processing route.
SPS can lower the required preparation temperature of single-phase ZrB2 below 2300 °C.
SPS can reduce holes and eventual ZrB2 component failure caused by prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The proposed SPS window is 1800–2000 °C at 50 MPa for 30 minutes.
SPS will densify and refine the microstructure of single-phase ZrB2.
Applied pressure and electrical current during SPS enhance diffusion in ZrB2.
Applied pressure and electrical current during SPS enhance grain growth in ZrB2.
The SPS intervention will reduce the preparation temperature by at least 200 °C relative to conventional preparation.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will attain a relative density of at least 98%.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have better structural integrity than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
Preparation below 1800 °C or above 2000 °C lies outside the stated preparation boundary.
Liquid-plating-bath exposure beyond 100 hours lies outside the stated service boundary.
The optimum SPS parameters and resulting microstructure may depend on the equipment and material.
The proposed experiment varies SPS temperature and liquid-plating-bath exposure time and measures relative density and microstructure by SEM and XRD.
The hypothesis is falsified if relative density is below 95%.
The hypothesis is falsified if significant porosity or degradation is observed after 100 hours in the liquid plating bath.

contradictions.description: Microstructure refinement generally implies retention or production of a finer grain structure, whereas the stated mechanism invokes enhanced grain growth, which tends toward coarsening; the hypothesis does not reconcile these effects.
